articles.title: RB D'Andre Swift becomes latest key Bears player to earn a big extension
articles.summary: The Bears and RB D'Andre Swift have agreed to a three-year extension worth $33.75 million.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have locked up another key player long term.

The Bears and running back D'Andre Swift have agreed to a three-year extension worth $33.75 million, which includes $27.5 million in guaranteed money, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Swift, 27, was a critical offensive piece for head coach Ben Johnson and the Bears, who went 11-6 and won the NFC North last season. He rushed for 1,087 yards and nine TDs last season and caught 34 passes for 299 yards and another score.

Swift and Johnson first worked together with the Detroit Lions , who drafted Swift in Round 2 of the 2020 NFL Draft. He was traded to the Eagles in 2023 and then signed a three-year, $24 million contract with the Bears in March 2024. His contract had been scheduled to expire following the 2026 season prior to signing the new extension.

The Bears have been busy this offseason restructuring contracts and taking care of some of their own key players long term.

After reworking the deals of Jonah Jackson and Cole Kmet in April, creating more than $10 million in salary-cap space, the Bears extended right tackle Darnell Wright in August, making him the highest-paid right tackle by average annual value with a four-year, $116 million extension through 2031 that included about $93 million in guaranteed money.

The Bears also recently created more cap room by restructuring the deals of Joe Thuney , Dayo Odeyingbo and T.J. Edwards , freeing up about $17 million for the 2026 books. That allowed the Bears to get under the cap, and it gave them enough room to extend Swift prior to the start of the regular season.

The Bears kick off the season in Week 1 at the Carolina Panthers at 1 p.m. ET Sunday on Fox.

articles.title: Carson Beck's Development Plan Detailed by Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur With Jacoby Brissett As QB1
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur discussed how the team plans to develop rookie quarterback Carson Beck while he sits at No. 3 on the depth chart behind starter Jacoby Brissett during the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur discussed how the team plans to develop rookie quarterback Carson Beck while he sits at No. 3 on the depth chart behind starter Jacoby Brissett during the 2026 season.

LaFleur explained Friday that Beck and backup passer Gardner Minshew II will split scout-team reps throughout the week leading up to games instead of Minshew solely handling scout-team duties, per ESPN's Josh Weinfuss.

"As you're trying to develop these guys, we just thought it was right to do that," LaFleur said. "If had Gardner been a second-year guy and was our No. 2, then probably wouldn't be doing this. But because he has played so much football, so much meaningful football in this league, understands this system, obviously took all the reps through OTAs, took a ton of reps in training camp, that's why we felt comfortable being able to do this."

Arizona selected Beck with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft following a senior season at Miami in which he helped the Hurricanes appear in the College Football Playoff national championship game.

In 16 starts last season, he completed 72.4 percent of his throws for 3,813 yards and 30 touchdowns compared to 12 interceptions.

It's understandable that the Cardinals want to keep Beck involved in practice throughout the regular season, as he was limited to just one preseason appearance due to a rib injury .

The 23-year-old performed admirably in his lone preseason contest, finishing 15-of-19 for 188 yards and one touchdown without getting picked off.

Still, Brissett will start under center when the Cardinals begin their 2026 campaign against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Kickoff is at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Chris Johnson's Titans Ring of Honor Ceremony Postponed Due to 'Unforeseen Circumstances'
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans' ceremony to induct former running back Chris Johnson into the team's Ring of Honor has been postponed.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans' ceremony to induct former running back Chris Johnson into the team's Ring of Honor has been postponed.

"Due to unforeseen circumstances, Chris Johnson and his family are no longer able to travel to Nashville for this Sunday's game," the Titans said in a statement released Friday. "Knowing how much he and his family desire to be in person at Nissan Stadium for his induction into the Titans Ring of Honor, we will postpone the official induction ceremony and look forward to celebrating the moment with them at a future date. Sunday's halftime ceremony will remain dedicated to celebrating Chris' incredible on-field achievements and legacy with our team. Our thoughts, along with those of Titans fans everywhere, continue to be with Chris and his wife, Brittany."

The ceremony was initially scheduled to take place during halftime of Tennessee's Week 1 clash with the New York Jets on Sunday.

Johnson previously announced that he had been diagnosed with ALS on June 29.

In an interview with Good Morning America 's Michael Strahan, he revealed that he was diagnosed with the disease in 2025.

"I want people to understand just how quickly ALS can attack your body," Johnson told Strahan. "Just over a year ago, I was picking up my 7-year-old daughter so she'd make a wish with her birthday cake. Today, I couldn't do that."

Tennessee eventually announced plans to induct Johnson into the team's Ring of Honor on July 17.

"Chris Johnson holds a special place in the hearts of our organization and our fans," Titans controlling owner Amy Adams Strunk said as part of the announcement. "His stats speak for themselves, and he will forever remain a leader in our record books, but the man behind the yardage deserves just as much celebration."

Johnson played 10 seasons in the NFL from 2008-17, with his first six occurring as a member of the Titans.

He surpassed 1,000 rushing yards in each year that he spent with Tennessee, including a 2009 campaign in which he picked up a league-leading 2,006 yards on the ground. Johnson is one of just nine running backs in NFL history to rush for at least 2,000 yards in a single season.

He amassed 7,965 rushing yards and 50 rushing touchdowns during his overall tenure on the Titans, with both totals ranking No. 4 on the team's all-time leaderboards .

Now, Johnson's Ring of Honor induction ceremony will take place later in the 2026 season.

articles.title: Dolphins vs. Raiders Week 1 Preview: Two Teams Begin New Eras in Las Vegas
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders will open their 2026 seasons Sunday afternoon in a matchup featuring two teams entering completely different chapter...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders will open their 2026 seasons Sunday afternoon in a matchup featuring two teams entering completely different chapters.

Miami will travel to Allegiant Stadium for a 1:25 p.m. PT kickoff on FOX. The Dolphins enter the season with a new head coach and quarterback, while Las Vegas begins the Klint Kubiak era with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins under center.

The Dolphins will turn to Malik Willis at quarterback after moving on from Tua Tagovailoa during the offseason.

Willis spent the previous two seasons with Green Bay and showed flashes of his ability as both a passer and runner. Miami is hoping the athletic quarterback can provide stability while Jeff Hafley begins his first season as head coach.

The Dolphins also have one of the NFL's youngest rosters, with 13 rookies making up nearly a quarter of the active roster.

The biggest weapon on offense will be running back De'Von Achane. After signing a new four-year contract, Achane enters the season as one of Miami's most important players and could see a heavy workload against a Raiders defense that struggled to stop the run last season.

The Raiders will counter with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins.

Cousins was brought in to provide experience while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza develops. Mendoza is currently behind Cousins on the depth chart, making the veteran quarterback's performance particularly important to the Raiders' hopes of getting off to a fast start.

Cousins will have running back Ashton Jeanty available after the second-year back returned to full practice following an ankle injury. Jeanty could be one of the biggest factors in the game.

Las Vegas will be without one of its biggest offensive stars.

Tight end Brock Bowers underwent knee surgery and is expected to miss the season opener, leaving Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas to handle the tight end responsibilities. Bowers' absence removes a major target from Cousins' offense.

That could put even more pressure on Jeanty and the Raiders' running game.

Meanwhile, Maxx Crosby remains the centerpiece of a Las Vegas defense that will need to create pressure against Willis.

The biggest matchup will be De'Von Achane against the Raiders' defense .

Miami ranked 13th in the NFL in rushing last season, while Las Vegas finished 32nd. If Achane can break loose early, the Dolphins could control the tempo and keep pressure off Willis.

On the other side, Miami's defense must prevent Jeanty from taking over. If the Raiders can establish their running game, Cousins should have opportunities to make plays downfield.

This is a difficult game to predict because both teams are still trying to establish new identities.

The Raiders have home-field advantage and a more experienced quarterback, while Miami has the more explosive running back and enters the game with plenty to prove.

Expect a physical opener in Las Vegas, with Cousins making enough plays late to give Kubiak his first victory as Raiders head coach.

articles.title: Why Levi Onwuzurike’s Lions Release May Be Temporary
articles.summary: The Lions released Levi Onwuzurike, but an NFL salary rule could explain why Detroit may bring the veteran defensive lineman back quickly.
articles.body:
Levi Onwuzurike 's release from the Detroit Lions on Friday looked, at first glance, like the end of his time in Detroit.

Dave Birkett raised a much more interesting possibility after the move: Detroit could be using the calendar and NFL contract rules to avoid guaranteeing Onwuzurike's entire 2026 base salary, then bring him back almost immediately.

That possibility deserves attention because Onwuzurike is a vested veteran entering the season on a $1.215 million base salary with no existing salary guarantee , according to Over the Cap's contract breakdown .

Detroit had already surprised some observers by keeping Onwuzurike on the initial 53-man roster after an offseason in which his future was anything but secure.

Now the Lions may simply be manipulating the timing of that roster spot.

Why Week 1 Changes the Financial Equation

The key is the NFL's termination-pay rule.

Under Article 30 of the NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement , a veteran with at least four credited seasons who makes his team's active/inactive list for the first regular-season game can become eligible for termination pay covering the unpaid balance of his base salary if he is later released.

In simpler terms, keeping Onwuzurike on the active roster Sunday could expose Detroit to paying his full $1.215 million salary even if it decided several weeks later that it no longer needed him.

Releasing him beforehand removes that Week 1 protection.

That makes Birkett's theory entirely plausible from a roster-management standpoint. Pride of Detroit's analysis of the move also raised the possibility that Onwuzurike could return quickly rather than treating Friday's transaction as an obvious goodbye.

This kind of maneuver is not unprecedented around the NFL. Teams have long waited until after the opener to sign vested veterans because the financial exposure changes once Week 1 passes.

Detroit has a reason to care about that with Onwuzurike in particular.

His injury history is not exactly a footnote.

Here is where the scenario gets particularly interesting.

Because Onwuzurike is a vested veteran, Detroit could theoretically sign him to the practice squad Saturday. Current NFL roster rules allow teams to temporarily elevate up to two practice-squad players for a game, which can increase the active/inactive roster to 54 or 55 players. NFL Football Operations explains the standard-elevation mechanism .

That means one possible sequence looks like this:

Detroit releases Onwuzurike Friday, signs him to the practice squad Saturday, elevates him for Sunday against New Orleans , then decides what to do with him after Week 1.

He could conceivably play Sunday without being on the 53-man roster in the way that would trigger the same termination-pay protection.

That is a remarkably specific piece of roster accounting, but Brad Holmes has never been shy about using every available mechanism.

And Detroit has extra incentive to maintain flexibility after Onwuzurike's medical history. His career has already included major back problems and a torn ACL, and his availability was a central reason he entered the offseason as a legitimate Lions roster bubble candidate .

There is one problem with the clever-contract-theory interpretation.

Detroit might simply prefer other defensive linemen.

The Lions are deeper up front than they have been in years, with Alim McNeill , Tyleik Williams , Mekhi Wingo , Derrick Moore , D.J. Wonnum , Tyler Lacy , Skyler Gill-Howard, Ahmed Hassanein and Eric O'Neill among the options surrounding Aidan Hutchinson .

Onwuzurike's 2024 season showed why Detroit kept betting on him. His physical traits can still create interior pressure when he is healthy. The question is how much confidence the Lions have that he will stay healthy and outperform younger, cheaper options.

But until Saturday's practice-squad moves arrive, I would not close the book.

articles.title: Titans delay Chris Johnson's Ring of Honor ceremony because of his family's travel issues
articles.summary: Chris Johnson’s Ring of Honor ceremony with the Tennessee Titans is on hold because of what the team described as unforeseen circumstances preventing his fam...
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Chris Johnson 's Ring of Honor ceremony with the Tennessee Titans is on hold because of what the team described as unforeseen circumstances preventing his family from traveling to Nashville in time for Sunday's game.

The Titans had expected to induct the 2009 NFL rushing leader at halftime of their season opener Sunday against the New York Jets . Johnson announced in June that he was diagnosed last year with ALS, a neurodegenerative condition commonly known as Lou Gehrig's disease that affects nerve cell communication with muscles throughout the body.

Titans officials announced the change of plans Friday.

"Knowing how much he and his family desire to be in person at Nissan Stadium for his induction into the Titans Ring of Honor, we will postpone the official induction ceremony and look forward to celebrating the moment with them at a future date," the Titans said in a statement on social media.

Titans officials said Sunday's halftime ceremony will remain dedicated to celebrating Johnson's on-field achievements and legacy.

Johnson, who turns 41 on Sept. 23, spent six seasons with the Titans after they selected him out of East Carolina with the 24th pick in the 2008 draft.

He earned the nickname "CJ2K" in 2009 when he finished with 2,006 yards rushing to join O.J. Simpson, Eric Dickerson, Barry Sanders, Terrell Davis and Jamal Lewis in the exclusive 2,000-yard club. He was the Associated Press NFL offensive player of the year that season.

Johnson also had 2,509 yards from scrimmage in 2009, a single-season record that still stands in the NFL.

He rushed for 7,965 yards and had 58 total touchdowns with the Titans. He ran for 9,651 yards and scored 64 touchdowns (55 rushing, 9 receiving) during a 10-year career that also included stops with the New York Jets (2014) and Arizona Cardinals (2015-17).

articles.title: 49ers' Kyle Shanahan, approaching franchise history, reportedly gets extension
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was already signed through the 2028 season, but a report emerged that he's now under contract farther into the f...
articles.body:
It appears Kyle Shanahan will pass Bill Walsh. And keep on going and going.

The San Francisco 49ers head coach signed a contract extension in the offseason, Netflix's Tom Pelissero reported, although his previous deal – that owner Jed York said on March 30 that he was through 2028 – wasn't close to expiring. The length of this new deal has not yet been disclosed.

"I think Kyle's got three years left (on his contract)," York said then. "I want Kyle to be here for a long time. He's been here for a long time. I want him to be here even longer."

Shanahan, 46, will match Walsh as the longest-tenured 49ers head coach if he finishes his 10th season with the team in 2026. Shanahan and the Rams' Sean McVay are the NFL's second-longest tenured head coaches. They trail only Kansas City 's Andy Reid, who is in his 14th season with the Chiefs.

Shanahan has an 83-67 regular-season record with the 49ers and a 9-5 mark in the postseason. His regular-season win total ranks third in franchise history behind George Seifert (98) and Walsh (92). His postseason total ranks third behind Seifert and Walsh, who each have 10. Shanahan's playoff winning percentage (.643) ranks ninth in NFL history (minimum 10 games). In Shanahan's first nine seasons, the 49ers won two NFC titles, three NFC West crowns, made five playoff appearances and had four 12-win seasons.

General manager John Lynch is also in his 10th season with the 49ers. York said in March that he believed Lynch was signed through 2027.

"I want (Lynch) to be here for a long time," York said. "But it's really what do those guys (Shanahan and Lynch) want to do? When you sit down and have conversations after 10 years, 'Where do you want to be? What is your life like? … Do you want to re-up to be part of the 49ers? Do you want to do something else in our organization in a different place?'

"I don't know the answer. I have a great relationship with both those guys. And I hope they're here and they're with me and the 49ers and our family for a very long time."
